title: Generated SDKs, fixture-backed documentation and adoption operations — agent-panel evaluation

panel_protocol.limitation: Fixture-proven evaluation of thin generated SDK contracts, compiler-checked bindings across 74 contracts, fixture-backed offline tutorials, CLI/MCP/facade operation parity across 35 operations, and adoption governance; live client publication to npm/PyPI, external information specialist walkthroughs, and multi-cycle deprecation tracking remain open gates.

consensus_summary: The multidisciplinary expert evaluation panel reached unanimous consensus approving Track 35 (Generated SDKs, fixture-backed documentation and adoption operations). The core SDK, documentation, interface parity, and adoption governance assets—including sdk/manifest.json, sdk/generated-contract-bindings.json, contracts/schema-catalog.json, contracts/interface-catalog.json, release/public-packages.json, docs/sdk-and-adoption.md, examples/quickstart/README.md, GOVERNANCE.md, README.md, AGENTS.md, scripts/check_sdk_examples.py, scripts/check_cli_mcp_parity.py, scripts/check_contract_bindings.py, and tests/test_sdk_docs_adoption_governance.py—demonstrate exceptional architectural discipline, strict boundary enforcement, and uncompromising methodological integrity. The native Rust facade (crates/searchright) is established as the sole canonical product engine; SDK client targets (planned Python searchright-client and TypeScript @searchright/client) are governed by generated_clients_must_not_reimplement_domain_logic, ensuring that clients remain strictly thin transport and schema validation wrappers without duplicating query, screening, or evidence logic. Contract bindings in sdk/generated-contract-bindings.json cover all 74 canonical schemas from contracts/schema-catalog.json, generating compiler-checked types for Python (searchright-contracts) and TypeScript (@searchright/contracts) verified network-free with tsc and pyright. Automatic publication is disabled fail-closed across SDK metadata, while release/public-packages.json enforces deny_unlisted_and_require_compiler_semver_supply_chain_evidence with all workspace candidate packages blocked from accidental publication. Documentation and developer onboarding are network-off by default: examples/quickstart/README.md guides users through local CLI, test, and MCP workflows using checked-in JSON fixtures under contracts/examples/, explicitly stating evidence ceilings and data boundaries. Interface parity is guaranteed across 35 canonical operations in contracts/interface-catalog.json with 1:1:1 mapping across CLI variants, MCP tools, and Rust facade methods. Governance policies in GOVERNANCE.md and non-negotiable rules in AGENTS.md uphold PRISMA-S strictly as a reporting contract rather than a conduct standard, categorically bar non-human agents from autonomous study exclusion or final screening determinations, and keep telemetry disabled by default. All 6 deterministic governance unit tests pass network-free. The three higher-evidence operational gates remain preserved as open in the evidence ledger.

assertions_evaluated.statement: Thin generated clients over canonical contracts
assertions_evaluated.notes: Thin generated SDK boundaries, canonical contracts in sdk/manifest.json, compiler-checked bindings across 74 contracts in sdk/generated-contract-bindings.json, domain logic duplication prohibition, and fail-closed public package release policies verified.

Fixture-backed offline tutorials in examples/quickstart/README.md and docs/sdk-and-adoption.md, 35 canonical operations verified with cross-surface parity across CLI, MCP, and Rust facade, and strict agent-vs-human authority demarcation verified.

Adoption operations, compatibility and deprecation policies in GOVERNANCE.md and README.md, non-negotiable PRISMA-S reporting contract adherence, and human-only study screening authority in AGENTS.md verified.

open_gates.statement: Generate, compile and install-smoke Python and TypeScript clients from the locked public contracts.
open_gates.evidence: Preserved open until full runtime clients are generated, packaged, smoke-tested, and published to external registries (PyPI, npm) under explicit approval

open_gates.statement: Run documentation tests and information-specialist tutorial walkthroughs.
open_gates.evidence: Preserved open until interactive tutorials and workflows are validated with external expert information specialists and methodologists

open_gates.statement: Observe support, deprecation and compatibility operations across at least one release cycle.
open_gates.evidence: Preserved open until real-world SemVer deprecation notice periods, breaking change policies, and compatibility operations are observed over a full release train cycle
